description:
How are Americans buying $80,000 trucks on a $70,000 salary? The short answer is many of them can’t actually afford them.

New vehicle prices have surged since 2019, with the average full-size truck now costing around $65,000. At the same time, nearly 1 in 5 new auto loans carries a monthly payment above $1,000. Dealers found a way to make those prices look manageable. Stretch the loan.
72- and 84-month financing can dramatically lower the monthly payment while keeping borrowers locked into debt for six or seven years. The trade-off is thousands of dollars in additional interest while the vehicle rapidly loses value. That creates another problem. Negative equity.
Millions of drivers now owe more than their cars are worth. When they trade in, default, or have the vehicle repossessed, the remaining debt doesn’t necessarily disappear. title: How Are Americans Affording $80,000 Trucks on $70,000 Salary

author: The Infographics Show
description:
At 25 years old, Leopold Aschenbrenner controlled one of the hottest AI hedge funds on Wall Street. Then roughly $35 Billion disappeared in days.

His fund had made huge leveraged bets on AI infrastructure companies like CoreWeave, Bloom Energy, and semiconductor stocks. As long as AI stocks kept rising, the strategy produced spectacular returns. But leverage works both ways. When the portfolio dropped sharply in July 2026, Goldman Sachs, JPMorgan, and Bank of America issued margin calls. Aschenbrenner suddenly needed billions in cash and was forced to liquidate his public portfolio. Citadel stepped in and bought the assets at a discount. Then many of those same stocks immediately rebounded.

The AI thesis may not have been the problem, the leverage was.
